summary: Tranylcypromine is a non-selective, irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) indicated for major depressive disorder in adults who have not responded adequately to other antidepressants. It is not first-line because of the risk of serious adverse reactions and drug interactions and the need for dietary tyramine restriction. It carries a boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behaviors and for hypertensive crisis precipitated by significant tyramine intake or certain drugs. Strict dietary counseling and avoidance of a long list of contraindicated medications are essential.
indications: Major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults who have not responded adequately to other antidepressants
Not indicated for initial treatment of MDD due to serious adverse reaction/interaction risk and required dietary restrictions

dosage.d: Recommended 30 mg per day in divided doses
dosage.n: Reserved for patients unresponsive to other antidepressants

dosage.d: Increase by 10 mg/day every 1 to 3 weeks to a maximum of 30 mg twice daily (60 mg/day)
dosage.n: Use more gradual increases in patients at risk for hypotension (e.g., geriatric)
Gradual discontinuation reduces risk of withdrawal effects

dosage.d: Allow 4 to 5 half-lives of the prior drug/active metabolite to elapse before starting
dosage.n: After stopping an MAOI, wait at least 14 days before starting tranylcypromine

dosage.d: Allow at least 14 days after stopping tranylcypromine before starting
dosage.n: Effect persists due to irreversible MAO inhibition

admin: Provide written tyramine dietary restrictions before starting and reinforce throughout therapy
Review all current and planned medications for contraindicated interactions before each prescription
Allow appropriate medication-free intervals when switching to or from contraindicated drugs
Monitor for emergence of suicidal thoughts/behaviors, especially early and at dose changes
moa: The antidepressant mechanism is not fully understood but is presumed to result from potentiation of central monoamine neurotransmitter activity through irreversible inhibition of the enzyme monoamine oxidase (MAO), which normally metabolizes monoamine neurotransmitters such as norepinephrine, serotonin, and dopamine.

absolute: Concomitant use, or use in rapid succession, with other MAOIs, SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclic antidepressants, and numerous other antidepressants/drugs (see full prescribing information)
Use with foods/beverages of high tyramine content
relative: Cardiovascular disease, hypertension, or history of headache
History of liver disease or abnormal liver function tests
monitor: Suicidal ideation and behavior, especially in young adults
Signs of serotonin syndrome when interacting drugs are involved

preg: There are limited data on use in pregnancy. Tranylcypromine is not approved for pediatric patients. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; untreated depression also carries risk. Discontinue gradually if therapy is stopped to avoid withdrawal effects in the patient.
lact: There are limited data on the presence of tranylcypromine in human milk and on effects on the breastfed infant. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: Use with caution; no specific dosage adjustment is provided in labeling.
hepatic: Contraindicated in patients with a history of liver disease or with abnormal liver function tests; hepatotoxicity has been associated with MAOIs.

major: Serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, triptans, tramadol, meperidine, linezolid) - serotonin syndrome; contraindicated
Sympathomimetics, amphetamines, decongestants (pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine) - hypertensive crisis; contraindicated
Other MAOIs - additive MAO inhibition and severe reactions; contraindicated
moderate: Antihypertensives - exaggerated or unpredictable blood pressure effects
Insulin and oral hypoglycemics - potentiated hypoglycemia
interactions.food: Avoid foods and beverages with high tyramine content (aged cheeses, cured/fermented meats, fermented soy products, tap/draft beer, sauerkraut, overripe fruits) to prevent hypertensive crisis.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcoholic beverages; many contain tyramine and alcohol adds CNS depression.
interactions.diagnostics: May interfere with tests; correct electrolyte abnormalities and review interacting drugs before procedures.

serious: Hypertensive crisis (severe headache, palpitations, neck stiffness)
emergency: Hypertensive crisis with severe occipital headache - medical emergency

monitoring: Blood pressure regularly, with patient awareness of hypertensive crisis symptoms
Suicidal thoughts and behaviors, especially during initiation and dose changes
Liver function in patients with risk factors
Adherence to tyramine dietary restrictions and medication restrictions
counsel: Strictly avoid high-tyramine foods and drinks; you will be given a list
Do not take any new medicine, including over-the-counter cold/allergy remedies, without checking - many can cause dangerous reactions
Seek emergency care for severe headache, palpitations, neck stiffness, or chest pain
Watch for and report worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm
Rise slowly from sitting or lying to reduce dizziness
Do not stop the medicine abruptly; it must be tapered
pk: Antidepressant effect may take days to weeks
Rapidly absorbed; peak plasma within about 1 to 2 hours
Plasma half-life about 2 hours, but MAO inhibition is irreversible and outlasts the drug
Enzyme inhibition persists until new MAO is synthesized (about 1 to 2 weeks)
Store per product labeling at controlled room temperature
pearls: Effect outlasts plasma half-life because MAO inhibition is irreversible - allow a 2-week washout when switching to/from interacting drugs
Hypertensive crisis from tyramine is the classic 'cheese reaction' - dietary counseling is mandatory
Reserved for treatment-resistant depression; not a first-line antidepressant
Carry an alert that you take an MAOI for emergency care providers
Concomitant serotonergic drugs can cause life-threatening serotonin syndrome
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take a double dose. Maintaining a steady schedule and never stopping abruptly is important.
overdose: Overdose may cause an initial period of agitation, hallucinations, hyperreflexia, and hyperpyrexia followed by cardiovascular instability with severe hypertension or hypotension, vascular collapse, seizures, and coma; effects may be delayed and prolonged. Provide intensive supportive care, control blood pressure and temperature, manage seizures, and monitor cardiac function for an extended period. There is no specific antidote. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
